learningObjectives.title: The CPU and von Neumann architecture

questions.q: What does the abbreviation CPU stand for?
options: Central Processing Unit
Central Program Utility
Computer Processing Unit
Core Processing Unit
questions.explain: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the component that processes all the data and instructions in a computer.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of the CPU?
options: To process data and instructions
To permanently store user files
To display graphics on the monitor
To connect the computer to the internet
questions.explain: The CPU's role is to fetch, decode and execute the instructions that make a program run.

questions.q: Which statement best describes a key feature of von Neumann architecture?
options: Instructions and data are stored together in the same memory
Instructions and data are stored in physically separate memories
Data is stored only in the CPU registers
Programs cannot be changed once loaded
questions.explain: In von Neumann architecture both program instructions and data share the same main memory.

questions.q: Which component of the CPU carries out arithmetic and logical operations?
options: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
The Control Unit (CU)
The cache
The Program Counter
questions.explain: The ALU performs calculations such as addition and logical comparisons like AND and OR.

questions.q: What is the role of the Control Unit (CU) within the CPU?
options: It coordinates and directs the activities of the CPU
It performs all arithmetic calculations
It provides long-term storage for programs
It stores the results of calculations
questions.explain: The Control Unit manages the flow of data around the CPU and controls the fetch-decode-execute cycle.

questions.q: What is the purpose of cache memory in the CPU?
options: To store frequently used instructions and data for fast access
To provide permanent storage when the computer is off
To perform logical operations
To hold the address of the next instruction
questions.explain: Cache is a small amount of very fast memory that reduces the time spent fetching data from slower RAM.

questions.q: What are the three stages of the CPU's main operating cycle?
options: Fetch, decode, execute
Read, write, store
Input, process, output
Load, run, save
questions.explain: The CPU continuously repeats the fetch-decode-execute cycle to run programs.

questions.q: What happens during the fetch stage of the fetch-decode-execute cycle?
options: An instruction is copied from memory into the CPU
The instruction is carried out by the ALU
The result is written back to memory
The instruction is translated into a set of signals
questions.explain: During fetch, the next instruction is retrieved from main memory and brought into the CPU.

questions.q: What happens during the decode stage of the cycle?
options: The instruction is interpreted to work out what needs to be done
The instruction is copied from RAM
The final result is stored in memory
The clock speed is increased
questions.explain: In the decode stage the Control Unit interprets the fetched instruction so the CPU knows which operation to perform.

questions.q: Which register holds the address of the next instruction to be executed?
options: The Program Counter (PC)
The Accumulator (ACC)
The Memory Data Register (MDR)
The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)
questions.explain: The Program Counter stores the memory address of the next instruction to be fetched.

questions.q: Which register stores the results of calculations carried out by the ALU?
options: The Accumulator (ACC)
The Memory Address Register (MAR)
The Program Counter (PC)
The cache
questions.explain: The Accumulator temporarily holds the results of arithmetic and logical operations performed by the ALU.

questions.q: What does the Memory Address Register (MAR) hold?
options: The address of the memory location to be read from or written to
The actual data being transferred to or from memory
The address of the next instruction
The result of the last calculation
questions.explain: The MAR stores the location in memory that is currently being accessed.

questions.q: What does the Memory Data Register (MDR) hold?
options: The data that has been read from or is to be written to memory
The address of a memory location
The next instruction's address
The clock speed of the CPU
questions.explain: The MDR temporarily stores the data being transferred between the CPU and main memory.

questions.q: In which unit is CPU clock speed measured?
options: Hertz (Hz)
Bytes (B)
Pixels (px)
Bits per second (bps)
questions.explain: Clock speed is measured in Hertz, usually gigahertz (GHz), representing cycles per second.

questions.q: How does increasing a CPU's clock speed generally affect its performance?
options: It can carry out more instructions per second
It permanently stores more data
It reduces the amount of RAM needed
It lowers the number of cores
questions.explain: A higher clock speed means more fetch-decode-execute cycles per second, so more instructions are processed.

questions.q: Why can a CPU with more cores improve performance?
options: Each core can process instructions independently at the same time
Each core increases the size of permanent storage
More cores reduce the clock speed needed
More cores replace the need for cache
questions.explain: Multiple cores allow the CPU to process several sets of instructions simultaneously.

questions.q: A CPU is described as running at 3.2 GHz. What does this mean?
options: It performs about 3.2 billion clock cycles per second
It has 3.2 gigabytes of cache
It contains 3.2 processing cores
It can store 3.2 billion instructions permanently
questions.explain: 3.2 GHz means 3.2 billion cycles per second, as 1 GHz equals one billion Hertz.

questions.q: A user often runs many programs at once and finds the computer slow at multitasking. Which upgrade would most directly help?
options: A CPU with more cores
A larger hard disk drive
A higher-resolution monitor
A faster internet connection
questions.explain: More cores let the CPU handle several programs simultaneously, improving multitasking performance.

questions.q: A program keeps re-using the same small set of data very frequently. Increasing which CPU feature would most reduce time spent fetching that data from RAM?
options: The size of the cache
The size of the hard drive
The resolution of the screen
The number of USB ports
questions.explain: A larger cache stores more frequently used data close to the CPU, cutting slow fetches from RAM.

questions.q: What is an embedded system?
options: A computer built into a larger device to perform a specific dedicated function
A general-purpose desktop computer
A cloud server used for storing files
A removable storage device
questions.explain: An embedded system is a computer within a larger device that carries out one dedicated task.

questions.q: Which of the following is the best example of an embedded system?
options: The controller inside a washing machine
A laptop running many applications
A desktop PC used for gaming
A web server hosting websites
questions.explain: A washing machine controller is dedicated to one task, which is characteristic of an embedded system.

questions.q: An engineer designs a control unit for a set of traffic lights. Why is an embedded system suitable for this?
options: It is dedicated to a single, specific function and does not need general-purpose flexibility
It needs to run a wide variety of user-installed applications
It requires a large monitor and keyboard for daily use
It must store the user's personal documents and photos
questions.explain: Traffic lights perform one fixed task, so a dedicated embedded system is efficient and reliable.
